service-management-001.question: Which of the following describes the approach of IT service management appropriately?
choices: The quality of an IT service is judged only from the provider's technical point of view, without considering its effect on the users' business
IT services that support the outcomes users want are delivered stably at the agreed quality and improved continually
The role of the IT service provider ends when a new system has been developed and put into operation
service-management-001.explanation: IT service management treats IT as a "service" and is the management approach for delivering services that help the outcomes of users' business stably, at the agreed quality and cost, and for continuing to improve them. The value of a service is determined by the balance between the outcomes users obtain and the costs and risks involved. ITIL is a widely referenced guide to putting this into practice around the world. Putting a system into operation is a beginning, and quality must be maintained and improved during operation.
choiceNotes: The value of a service is determined by the outcomes users obtain, so the effect on the users' business must be considered.
Correct. Services that support users' outcomes are delivered at the agreed quality and continually improved.
Putting a system into operation is a beginning; the subsequent operation and improvement are also the role of the IT service provider.

service-management-002.question: Which of the following is a document in which an IT service provider collects the list of IT services that users can choose and use, together with the description of each, its conditions of use, its standard service levels and how to request it or make inquiries?
choices: Service catalogue
Configuration management database (CMDB)
Record of known errors
service-management-002.explanation: A service catalogue describes, in terms users can understand, the list of IT services currently offered, their content, conditions of use, standard service levels, how to request them and so on. Users look at the catalogue to choose and request the services they need, and the provider concludes SLAs (service level agreements) based on it. A CMDB manages information about the equipment and software that make up services, and a record of known errors records problems whose causes or workarounds are known.
choiceNotes: Correct. It collects the list of services offered, their content, conditions of use and so on.
It is a database that manages the configuration items that make up services, such as hardware and software, and their relationships.
It records problems whose root cause or workaround is known; it is not a list of services.

service-management-003.question: To achieve the service levels promised to users in an SLA, an IT service provider agrees with the network operations department and other departments within the same organization on the content and level of the work each is responsible for. Which of the following is this agreement?
choices: SLA (service level agreement)
A contract with an external supplier
OLA (operational level agreement)
service-management-003.explanation: IT services are delivered through the cooperation of several departments within the organization, such as the service desk, server operations and network operations, and of outside companies. To keep the SLA with users, OLAs (operational level agreements) are made with the internal departments that support it and contracts with external suppliers, fixing the level of the work each one is responsible for. The targets of the OLAs and contracts are set so that the SLA targets can be achieved.
choiceNotes: An SLA is an agreement between the service provider and the users.
This is made with a supplier outside the organization (such as a telecommunications carrier), not with a department within the same organization.
Correct. It is an agreement between departments within the organization on the level of the work that supports the SLA.

service-management-004.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate service level item to agree on with users in the SLA for a company's internal expense reimbursement system?
choices: The monthly availability during service hours, 9:00 to 18:00 on weekdays, is at least 99.5%, and the results are reported every month
When a failure occurs, staff make every effort to recover as quickly as possible and report the outcome to users
Operations staff constantly keep learning about the latest technology trends and attend an external training course once a year
service-management-004.explanation: Service level items in an SLA are set so that they are meaningful to users and their results can be measured to judge whether they were achieved. Service hours, availability, the time from receiving a failure report to recovery, the time to answer inquiries and so on are defined with figures and measurement methods, and the results are reported regularly. An expression such as "as quickly as possible" does not allow anyone to judge whether it was met. Staff learning is important, but it is not an item of service quality agreed with users.
choiceNotes: Correct. The period covered, the numerical target of 99.5% and the reporting method are fixed, so achievement can be measured.
There is no numerical target, so it is impossible to judge whether it was met.
This is an internal effort of the provider, not an item of service quality agreed with users.

service-management-005.question: Which of the following is an appropriate activity of service level management?
choices: Once an SLA has been agreed, the results are not measured and the content is not reviewed during the contract period; operation simply continues as it is
Service level targets are decided by the provider alone, without agreement with users, and published at values that are easy to achieve
The results for the agreed service levels are measured regularly and reported to users, and for items that fall short of the targets, the causes are analyzed and improvements are made
service-management-005.explanation: Service level management is an activity that repeats a cycle: agreeing on service level targets based on user requirements, measuring and reporting the results, and reviewing them with users to make improvements. For items that fall short of their targets, the causes are analyzed and an improvement plan is drawn up. When users' business changes, the content of the SLA is also reviewed.
choiceNotes: Continuing to measure and report results and to review the content is at the core of service level management.
Service level targets are decided by agreement between users and the provider, based on user requirements.
Correct. Results are measured and reported, and items that do not reach their targets are improved.

service-management-006.question: The SLA for an internal system sets the service hours as 9:00 to 21:00 on weekdays (12 hours a day) and requires availability during service hours (the fraction of service hours during which the system was in operation) of at least 99.5%. Take a month as having 20 weekdays, and do not count outages outside service hours. Which of the following is the upper limit on the total outage time allowed within service hours in a month?
choices: 7.2 minutes
72 minutes
216 minutes
service-management-006.explanation: The service hours in a month are 12 × 20 = 240 hours. At 99.5% availability, 0.5% of that time may be lost, so the allowed outage time is 240 × 0.005 = 1.2 hours, that is, 72 minutes. 7.2 minutes takes 0.5% to be 0.05%, and 216 minutes applies 0.5% to all 24 hours of a 30-day month (720 hours) instead of to the service hours.
choiceNotes: This takes 0.5% to be 0.05% (240 hours × 0.0005 = 0.12 hours).
Correct. 240 hours × 0.005 = 1.2 hours = 72 minutes.
This is based on all 24 hours of a 30-day month (720 hours), which does not match the condition that outages outside service hours are not counted.

service-management-007.question: The SLA for a cloud service defines monthly availability = (scheduled service time − outage time due to failures) ÷ scheduled service time, where the scheduled service time is the total time in the month minus the time of planned maintenance announced in advance. If the monthly availability is at least 99.9%, there is no refund; if it is at least 99.0% but below 99.9%, 10% of the monthly fee is refunded; and if it is below 99.0%, 30% is refunded. Take a month as 30 days. In one month there were 120 minutes of planned maintenance and a total of 40 minutes of outages due to failures. Which of the following is the refund rate for this month?
service-management-007.explanation: The total time in a month is 30 × 24 × 60 = 43,200 minutes, and the scheduled service time, excluding the 120 minutes of planned maintenance, is 43,080 minutes. The monthly availability is (43,080 − 40) ÷ 43,080 ≈ 99.91%, which is at least 99.9%, so there is no refund (0%). Counting the planned maintenance as outage time as well, (43,200 − 160) ÷ 43,200 ≈ 99.63%, leads to the wrong conclusion of 10%. In an SLA, it is important to define clearly in advance how planned maintenance is treated and the formula for availability.
choiceNotes: This judgment uses an availability (about 99.63%) that counts the 120 minutes of planned maintenance as outage time and is based on the total of 43,200 minutes.
To fall below 99.0%, outages due to failures would have to exceed 430.8 minutes.

service-management-008.question: Which of the following is an appropriate way to decide the priority for handling incidents?
choices: To be fair, incidents are handled in the order they are received regardless of their content, and the order is never changed
Priority is decided by combining the size of the effect on the business (impact) and how pressing it is to resolve (urgency)
The higher the job title of the reporting user, the larger the effect on the business is assumed to be, and incidents are handled in that order
service-management-008.explanation: In incident management, a priority is set for each incident to decide the order of handling and the resources assigned, so that the effect on the business is kept as small as possible with limited staff. Priority is usually decided by combining the scope of the users and business affected (impact) with how quickly the incident must be resolved (urgency). Deciding by order of receipt or by the reporter's job title risks delaying the handling of failures that affect many users.
choiceNotes: If an incident with a large impact arrives later, its handling is delayed.
Correct. Priority is decided by the combination of impact and urgency.
The reporter's job title does not indicate the size of the effect on the business or the urgency.

service-management-009.question: The service desk received a call from a user saying, "In the expense reimbursement system, the submit button does not respond when I attach an image of a receipt." The same symptom is registered as a known error, with the recorded workaround "the image can be submitted if it is first registered from a separate registration screen." Which of the following is the most appropriate action in incident management?
choices: Ask the user to hold off on submitting expenses until the root cause is found and a permanent fix is completed
Have the service desk staff member guess the cause and fix the program in the production environment on the spot to prevent recurrence
Tell the user about the recorded workaround so that they can continue working, and log the incident and link it to the known error
service-management-009.explanation: The goal of incident management is to return the service to normal as quickly as possible and keep the effect on the business small. If a workaround is recorded for a known error, it is passed on so that the user can continue working. Logging the incident and linking it to the known error shows how often it occurs and provides input for judging the priority of a permanent fix. Resolving the root cause is done by problem management, and changes to the production environment go through change management.
choiceNotes: Making the user stop working when a workaround exists goes against the goal of restoring service quickly.
Changes to the production environment are made only after their impact has been assessed and they have been approved in change management.
Correct. The workaround lets the user keep working, and a record is kept.

service-management-010.question: Which of the following describes a "known error" in problem management appropriately?
choices: A problem whose root cause has been identified or for which a workaround is known, but whose permanent fix has not yet been completed
An incident caused by a user's operating mistake that was resolved by explaining the correct operation to the user
A defect found during development that was fixed and tested before release and does not remain in the production environment
service-management-010.explanation: In problem management, the not-yet-understood root cause behind one or more incidents is treated as a "problem". A problem whose root cause has been identified through investigation, or for which a workaround has been found, but whose permanent fix has not yet been completed is called a "known error", and it is recorded together with the workaround and shared with the service desk and others. This allows the workaround to be used immediately when the same incident occurs.
choiceNotes: Correct. It is a problem whose cause or workaround is known but whose permanent fix has not been completed.
Operating mistakes are one cause of incidents, but this is not the definition of a known error.
A defect that was fixed and released no longer remains in the production environment, so it is not managed as a known error.

service-management-011.question: A file server stops responding with the same error several times a week, and each time an operations staff member restarts it to restore service. From the standpoint of problem management, which of the following is an appropriate action?
choices: Since a restart restores service, do not treat it as a problem and keep restarting the server each time
Without knowing the cause, keep changing the settings of the production server one after another at the staff member's discretion to see what happens
Register the series of incidents as a problem, investigate the root cause, and carry out the permanent fix through change management
service-management-011.explanation: When the same incident keeps recurring, a root cause probably remains, so it is registered as a problem and investigated. Until the root cause is found, the restart is recorded as a workaround and shared as a known error. When a permanent fix changes the server's settings or programs, its impact and risk are assessed in change management and it is approved before being carried out.
choiceNotes: A restart is a temporary workaround; the cause remains, so the failures keep recurring.
Changing production settings without assessment or approval can cause new failures and makes it impossible to tell what actually worked.
Correct. The root cause is investigated, and the fix is carried out through change management.

service-management-012.question: Which of the following is an appropriate way to carry out change management?
choices: Changes to the production environment may be made at any time without keeping records, whenever the person in charge judges them necessary
Change requests are recorded, assessed for impact, risk and cost, and approved before being carried out according to plan
Changes are approved together after they have been carried out
service-management-012.explanation: Change management is the process for preventing failures caused by changes, in which changes to IT services and their components are recorded, assessed for impact, risk and cost, and approved before being carried out. Change requests are recorded when received and, depending on their content, reviewed at a meeting of the people concerned. After implementation, the result is checked, the change is recorded and the configuration management information is updated.
choiceNotes: Changes with no record or assessment cause failures and make it impossible to trace later what was changed.
Correct. Changes are carried out according to plan after being recorded, assessed and approved.
Approval comes before implementation. Approving afterward does not prevent failures caused by the change.

service-management-013.question: A serious security vulnerability has been found, and a patch must be applied to the production servers immediately. The regular meeting that reviews changes is two weeks away. Which of the following is the most appropriate response in change management?
choices: Because it is urgent, skip both approval and records, apply the patch immediately at the discretion of the person in charge, and report only if a problem occurs
Follow the normal procedure: review the impact and risk at the regular meeting two weeks from now, and apply the patch after it is approved

Follow the emergency change procedure defined in advance: a small group of authorized approvers quickly assesses and approves the change, it is applied, and the records are completed and reviewed afterward
service-management-013.explanation: Change management defines an emergency change procedure for changes that must be carried out urgently. Even for an emergency change, a small group of approvers with the authority to approve quickly assesses the impact and risk and approves it, and the change is applied after testing and a back-out procedure have been prepared as far as possible. If records and documents are completed after implementation, they are completed and reviewed afterward. If both approval and records are skipped, the cause cannot be traced when the change causes a failure.
choiceNotes: Approval and records are not skipped even in an emergency; the simplified emergency change procedure is used instead.
Waiting two weeks greatly increases the risk that the vulnerability will be exploited.
Correct. The change is approved quickly under the emergency change procedure, applied, and reviewed afterward.

service-management-014.question: Several approved changes are bundled into a release and deployed to the production environment. Which of the following is an appropriate way to carry out release management?
choices: A release that has been tested in an environment close to production is deployed after a deployment procedure and a back-out plan for returning to the original state on failure have been prepared
Because it was confirmed to work correctly in the development environment, testing in an environment close to production is skipped and the release is deployed at night when usage is low
A deployment procedure document is prepared, but the procedure for returning to the original state is worked out only after deployment, once a problem has occurred
service-management-014.explanation: In release management, a release that bundles approved changes is planned, tested in an environment close to production and deployed to the production environment by a set procedure. A back-out plan for returning to the original state is prepared in advance in case the deployment fails or a serious problem is found after deployment. After deployment, the result is checked and the configuration management information is updated.
choiceNotes: Correct. A tested release is deployed with a deployment procedure and a back-out plan prepared.
The development and production environments differ in settings, data volume, connected equipment and so on, so problems that occur only in production are missed.
Working out how to go back only after a problem occurs makes recovery slow and the impact large.

service-management-015.question: Which of the following describes a configuration item (CI) recorded in the CMDB (configuration management database) in configuration management appropriately?
choices: A table that totals the number of inquiries received by the service desk by month and by service
A component that is needed to deliver a service and is placed under management, such as hardware, software or a document, recorded together with its version, location and relationships with other CIs
Software that users buy personally and use for their work, and that the organization neither tracks nor manages
service-management-015.explanation: Configuration management is the process of identifying the components that make up IT services (configuration items, CIs) and recording their attributes and relationships with other CIs accurately, keeping them up to date. CIs include servers and network equipment, software and its versions, documents such as design documents and procedures, and the services themselves. Knowing the relationships between CIs makes it easier to determine the scope of a failure and the impact of a change.
choiceNotes: The number of inquiries is a record of service desk performance, not a configuration item.
Correct. It is a component under management whose attributes and relationships with other CIs are recorded.
Things the organization does not manage are not recorded as configuration items.

service-management-016.question: Which of the following is the main benefit of setting up a service desk as a single point of contact (SPOC) that receives all inquiries and failure reports from users?
choices: Users do not have to wonder whom to contact, and because all records of contacts are gathered in one place, it becomes easier to grasp the status of handling and trends
The service desk resolves the root causes of all failures itself, so specialist engineers are no longer needed
The number of inquiries itself falls and failures stop occurring
service-management-016.explanation: The service desk is the single point of contact (SPOC) between users and the IT service provider. Users do not have to look for different contacts depending on the matter, and since everything received is recorded, the progress of handling can be managed and the records can be used to analyze incident trends. Matters that the service desk cannot resolve are handed over to specialist technical teams.
choiceNotes: Correct. There is a single contact, and records are gathered so that the situation is easy to grasp.
Matters the service desk cannot resolve are handed to specialist technical teams, so specialist engineers are still needed.
Having a single contact does not make inquiries or failures themselves disappear.

service-management-017.question: An incident received by a service desk staff member was about to exceed the resolution target time set in the SLA. The staff member reported the situation to the service desk manager and asked for a decision on adding staff and on contacting users. Which of the following is this action?
choices: Functional escalation
Registering a problem with problem management
Hierarchical escalation
service-management-017.explanation: Escalation means handing an incident that the person in charge cannot handle alone over to another person or team, or asking for a decision. Handing it over to a technical team with the specialist knowledge or authority needed to resolve it is functional escalation, and reporting to higher management to ask for decisions or resources when the target time is about to be exceeded or the impact is large is hierarchical escalation. In this example the staff member reported to the manager and asked for decisions such as adding staff, so it is hierarchical escalation.
choiceNotes: This hands the handling over to a technical team with specialist knowledge; it does not ask higher management for a decision.
This registers a problem to investigate the root cause, which is a different activity from reporting when the target time is about to be exceeded.
Correct. It reports to higher management and asks for decisions and resources.

service-management-018.question: Which of the following is an appropriate activity of capacity management?
choices: When a failure occurs, using a recorded workaround to restart the service as quickly as possible
Monitoring CPU and storage utilization and so on, forecasting future demand, and securing the necessary processing capacity in a planned way at a cost that matches its value
Receiving and recording user inquiries and failure reports together at a single point of contact
service-management-018.explanation: Capacity management is the activity of securing, at an appropriate cost, processing capacity (CPU, memory, storage, network bandwidth and so on) that matches current and future business demand. Utilization and response times are monitored and trends analyzed, demand is forecast taking into account growth in users and plans for new business, and expansion is planned. Too little capacity causes slow responses or outages, and too much wastes money.
choiceNotes: This is an activity of incident management.
Correct. The necessary processing capacity is secured in a planned way, based on monitoring and demand forecasts.
This is the role of the service desk.

service-management-019.question: A storage system with a capacity of 10 TB currently holds 4 TB. Assume that usage grows every month by 5% of the previous month's usage (it grows like compound interest). After how many months will usage first reach 80% of capacity or more? Which of the following is the most appropriate?
choices: After 8 months
After 15 months
After 20 months
service-management-019.explanation: 80% is 8 TB, so we look for the smallest n such that 4 × 1.05ⁿ ≥ 8, that is, 1.05ⁿ ≥ 2. Since 4 × 1.05¹⁴ ≈ 7.92 TB and 4 × 1.05¹⁵ ≈ 8.32 TB, the answer is after 15 months (log 2 ÷ log 1.05 ≈ 14.2). After 8 months assumes growth of 5% of capacity (0.5 TB) every month, and after 20 months assumes a constant growth of 5% of the initial usage (0.2 TB) every month.
choiceNotes: This assumes growth of 5% of the 10 TB capacity (0.5 TB) every month.
Correct. 4 × 1.05¹⁵ ≈ 8.32 TB, so usage first reaches 8 TB or more after 15 months.
This assumes a constant growth of 5% of the initial 4 TB (0.2 TB) every month and ignores the compound growth.

service-management-020.question: During 30 days (720 hours) of operation, a system failed 3 times, and the total outage time due to the failures was 6 hours. Which of the following is the MTBF (mean time between failures) calculated from the results for this period?
choices: 238 hours
240 hours
714 hours
service-management-020.explanation: MTBF is the total operating time divided by the number of failures. The operating time is 720 − 6 = 714 hours, so MTBF is 714 ÷ 3 = 238 hours. MTTR (mean time to repair) is 6 ÷ 3 = 2 hours, and the availability is 238 ÷ (238 + 2) ≈ 0.992, which equals 714 ÷ 720. 240 hours divides 720 hours by 3 without subtracting the outage time, and 714 hours is not divided by the number of failures.
choiceNotes: Correct. (720 − 6) ÷ 3 = 238 hours.
This divides 720 hours by 3 without subtracting the 6 hours of outage.
This is the total operating time, not divided by the number of failures.

service-management-021.question: A system has an MTBF (mean time between failures) of 500 hours, and the availability target in its SLA is at least 99.5%. Assuming the MTBF does not change and calculating availability = MTBF ÷ (MTBF + MTTR), which of the following is closest to the maximum MTTR (mean time to repair) that meets the target?
choices: 1.5 hours
2.5 hours
3.6 hours
service-management-021.explanation: Solving 500 ÷ (500 + MTTR) ≥ 0.995 gives MTTR ≤ 500 × 0.005 ÷ 0.995 ≈ 2.51 hours, so the maximum is about 2.5 hours. With 1.5 hours, the availability is 500 ÷ 501.5 ≈ 0.997, which meets the target, but it is not the maximum. 3.6 hours is the total outage time allowed in a 720-hour month (720 × 0.005), not the repair time per failure. Monitoring that detects failures quickly, spare parts on hand, well-prepared procedures and automatic switchover are effective in shortening the MTTR.
choiceNotes: This meets the target but is not the largest value allowed.
Correct. MTTR ≤ 500 × 0.005 ÷ 0.995 ≈ 2.51 hours.
This is the total outage time allowed in a month (720 hours), mistaken for the repair time per failure. With an MTTR of 3.6 hours, the availability would be about 0.993.

service-management-022.question: Which of the following is an appropriate way to draw up a business continuity plan (BCP)?
choices: Since every business activity is indispensable, aim to recover all business activities and systems with the same priority and within the same time
Writing up the plan and distributing it to everyone is enough, so costly exercises and reviews of the plan are not needed

Analyze the impact on the business to determine the critical activities to be continued or recovered first and the acceptable downtime, set recovery targets and procedures for the systems that support them, and keep exercising and reviewing the plan
service-management-022.explanation: A BCP is a plan for continuing critical business activities, or resuming them quickly, even when a disaster or large-scale failure occurs. First, the impact on the business is analyzed (business impact analysis) to determine the critical activities and their acceptable downtime, and targets such as the recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO) are set for the systems that support them. Exercises confirm whether the plan actually works, and it keeps being reviewed as the organization and its systems change. This ongoing cycle of drawing up, exercising and reviewing the plan is called business continuity management (BCM).
choiceNotes: Trying to recover everything with the same priority spreads limited resources thin and delays the resumption of critical activities.
Without exercises, it is unknown whether the plan actually works, and it cannot keep up with changes in the organization.
Correct. Impact analysis determines the critical activities and targets, and exercises and reviews continue.

service-management-023.question: Which of the following describes a double-conversion (online) UPS (uninterruptible power supply) appropriately?
choices: Even in normal operation it converts the utility power to DC and then back to AC with an inverter before supplying it, so there is no momentary interruption from switching during a power outage, and it is less affected by voltage and frequency fluctuations
In normal operation it supplies the utility power directly and switches to supply from the inverter after detecting an outage, so a brief interruption can occur at the moment of switching
As long as fuel keeps being supplied, it can continue to supply power no matter how many days an outage lasts
service-management-023.explanation: A double-conversion (online) UPS converts utility power to DC with a rectifier and, while charging its battery, always supplies stable AC produced by its inverter. Even during an outage, the inverter simply continues to be fed from the battery, so there is no momentary interruption from switching, and disturbances in voltage or frequency are hardly passed on to the equipment; for this reason it is widely used for servers. On the other hand, because it is always converting power, its losses are larger than those of a standby (offline) UPS. Long outages are covered by a generator that starts while the UPS is supplying power.
choiceNotes: Correct. Power always passes through the inverter, so there is no interruption during an outage.
This describes a standby (offline) UPS.
This describes a generator. The time a UPS can supply power is limited by the capacity of its battery.

service-management-024.question: Which of the following is an appropriate approach to fire suppression for the server rooms of a data center?
choices: Electronic equipment does not burn easily and there is little risk of fire, so no fire suppression system is needed in server rooms
Only ordinary sprinklers that spray large amounts of water are installed, cooling the equipment along with the fire to stop it spreading
To limit damage to equipment, a gas-based fire suppression system using inert gas or the like is used, with an alarm before discharge so that people can evacuate
service-management-024.explanation: In server rooms, extinguishing fires with water can spread equipment failures and data loss, so gas-based fire suppression systems using inert gas or similar agents are widely used. Because gas-based systems put out fires by such means as lowering the oxygen concentration, they are designed to sound an alarm before discharge and release the gas after the people in the room have evacuated. They are combined with detectors that sense smoke at an early stage to keep damage small.
choiceNotes: Fires can start in cable insulation, power equipment and the like, so a fire suppression system is necessary.
Large amounts of water can damage equipment that the fire has not reached and spread the damage.
Correct. A gas-based system is used, and people are evacuated before discharge.

service-management-025.question: Which of the following describes the purpose of a systems audit appropriately?
choices: From an independent, professional standpoint, to inspect and evaluate whether controls over the risks associated with information systems are properly designed and operated, and to communicate the results to the parties concerned as assurance or advice
To join an information system development project, write and test programs personally, and speed up development
To direct the recovery work when a failure occurs in an information system and personally carry out measures to prevent recurrence
service-management-025.explanation: A systems audit is an activity in which specialist auditors independent of the audited area inspect and evaluate whether controls (management mechanisms) over the risks of information systems are properly designed and operated. The results are reported to management and other parties as assurance that there are no problems or as advice for improvement (improvement recommendations). If auditors carried out development or operations work themselves, they would be evaluating their own work and their independence would be impaired.
choiceNotes: Correct. It inspects and evaluates from an independent standpoint and provides assurance or advice.
This is development work itself, not an audit. An auditor who took part would lose independence.
Recovery from failures is the role of the operations department.

service-management-026.question: From the standpoint of the independence of systems auditors, which of the following is the most appropriate person to audit a sales management system?
choices: An employee of the information systems department who developed the sales management system and is still responsible for its maintenance
A section manager in the sales department who uses the sales management system every day and manages the business
An employee of the internal audit department who is not involved in developing or operating the audited business or system
service-management-026.explanation: Systems auditors are required to be independent of what they audit. If people involved in developing, operating or using the audited area carry out the audit, they are evaluating their own work or their own department's work, so they may not judge objectively and will not appear fair to others. For this reason, the audit is assigned to employees of an internal audit department independent of the audited department, or to external auditors.
choiceNotes: This person would be evaluating a system they developed and maintain, so they are not independent.
This person is in a position of managing the audited business, so they are not independent.
Correct. This person is independent of the audited area.

service-management-027.question: Among the steps of a systems audit, which of the following is appropriately done in the preliminary survey?
choices: Summarizing the audit conclusions and preparing and submitting the audit report together with improvement recommendations
Reviewing documents and interviewing the people concerned to understand the actual state of the audited area, and deciding concretely on the audit procedures to be carried out in the main audit
Carrying out audit procedures to gather sufficient audit evidence and to firm up the basis for findings
service-management-027.explanation: A systems audit generally proceeds in the order of audit planning, preliminary survey, main audit, evaluation and conclusion, audit reporting and follow-up. In the preliminary survey, the auditor reviews documents such as rules, procedures and system configuration diagrams and interviews the people concerned to understand the actual state and risks of the audited area, and decides concretely on the audit procedures for the main audit. In the main audit, those procedures are carried out to gather audit evidence, which is then evaluated to reach a conclusion.
choiceNotes: This is done at the audit reporting stage.
Correct. It grasps the actual state of the audited area and makes the procedures for the main audit concrete.
This is done in the main audit.

service-management-028.question: A systems auditor made improvement recommendations in an audit report. Which of the following is an appropriate follow-up afterward?
choices: Checking whether the audited department is making improvements in line with the recommendations, and confirming the status of the improvements
The systems auditor modifies the audited department's system personally to complete the improvements
The audit report is not submitted to management until the improvements are finished
service-management-028.explanation: In the follow-up, the systems auditor checks whether the audited department is carrying out the improvements recommended as planned. Responsibility for making the improvements lies with the audited department (and the management directing it); if the auditor did the improvement work personally, they would later be evaluating their own results and their independence would be impaired. The audit report is submitted to management and others once the audit conclusions have been reached.
choiceNotes: Correct. Checking the status of the improvements is the follow-up.
Carrying out improvements is the responsibility of the audited department. If the auditor does it, independence is impaired.
The audit report is submitted once the conclusions are reached, and the status of improvements is checked in the follow-up.

service-management-029.question: A systems auditor is gathering audit evidence on whether the records of payments to business partners are correct. Which of the following is generally considered the audit evidence with the highest probative value?
choices: An oral explanation from a staff member of the audited department that "the processing is done correctly"
The result of matching the balance confirmation replies that the systems auditor obtained directly from the business partners against the system's records
A summary table of processing results newly prepared by the audited department for the audit
service-management-029.explanation: The probative value of audit evidence is generally considered higher when it is obtained from an independent party outside the audited department, when the auditor obtains or verifies it directly, and when it exists as documents or records rather than orally. The result of matching replies obtained directly by the auditor from the business partners against the system's records satisfies these conditions. An oral explanation, or a summary prepared by the audited department for the audit, is weak support on its own and must be confirmed with other evidence.
choiceNotes: An oral explanation leaves no record and is only the audited department's assertion, so its probative value is low.
Correct. Evidence obtained directly by the auditor from an outside party is matched against the records.
It is material prepared by the audited department, and without matching it to the original records it is weak support.

service-management-030.question: Which of the following describes an audit trail appropriately?
choices: A document in which the systems auditor records the procedures carried out in the audit, the evidence obtained and the conclusions
A document that summarizes the audit results and improvement recommendations and is submitted to management
Records that make it possible to trace and verify afterward the flow of processing from the occurrence of a transaction to its final recording, and who did what and when
service-management-030.explanation: An audit trail is a set of records that makes it possible to trace and verify afterward the flow of data from input through processing, output and storage, together with who operated on it and when. Access and operation logs, processing records and approval records are examples, and auditors follow the audit trail to verify that processing was legitimate and accurate. It is important to plan from the system design stage so that an audit trail is kept.
choiceNotes: This describes audit working papers.
This describes an audit report.
Correct. It is a set of records that lets the flow of processing and operations be traced afterward.

service-management-031.question: Among the techniques of systems auditing, which of the following describes the test data method appropriately?
choices: Test data prepared by the auditor are processed by the audited program, and the results are compared with the results predicted in advance to check whether the program processes correctly
Production data are processed by a program prepared by the auditor, and the results are compared with the processing results of the production system
A mechanism that writes out data midway through processing is built into a particular place in the audited program, and those data are examined
service-management-031.explanation: In the test data method, the auditor prepares test data that include both valid and invalid data (such as amounts over a limit), has the audited program process them, and checks whether the results are as predicted. It is suited to checking whether input checks and calculations are correctly built into the program. Processing production data with the auditor's program and comparing the results is parallel simulation, and writing out and examining data midway through processing is the snapshot method.
choiceNotes: Correct. Test data are processed and the results compared with the predicted results.
This describes parallel simulation.
This describes the snapshot method.

service-management-032.question: Which audit technique sets up a fictitious customer account for audit purposes in a sales system and processes audit data against that account at the same time as normal business processing, in order to check the results?
choices: Snapshot method
ITF method
Tracing method
service-management-032.explanation: The ITF (integrated test facility) method sets up fictitious accounts or departments for audit purposes in the production system and has audit data processed together with production processing, then checks the results. It allows continuous checking in the production environment as it is, but a procedure for removing the audit data afterward must be defined so that they do not affect production totals and the like. The snapshot method writes out and examines data midway through processing, and the tracing method traces and records the path along which a particular transaction was processed and examines it.
choiceNotes: This technique writes out and examines data midway through processing at particular places in a program.
Correct. Fictitious audit accounts are set up in the production system and audit data are processed against them.
This technique traces and examines the path along which a particular transaction was processed (such as the sequence of instructions executed).

service-management-033.question: A systems auditor used generalized audit software to extract duplicated invoice numbers and transactions over the approval limit from a year's worth of transaction data (several million records) in a sales system. Which of the following is an appropriate advantage of using computer-assisted audit techniques (CAAT) in this way?
choices: It can prove that a program has no errors without examining its internal logic
The extracted transactions can be concluded to be fraudulent, so no further checks are needed
Exceptional transactions that are easily missed by sampling, which examines only part of the data, can be extracted efficiently from all the records
service-management-033.explanation: CAAT is a collective term for techniques that perform audit procedures with computers, and it includes extracting and analyzing data with generalized audit software. Because it can extract the records that meet given conditions from all the data, even in large volumes, it makes it easier to find exceptional transactions that sampling of part of the data tends to miss. However, the extracted records are only candidates for examination, and whether they are fraud or errors must be confirmed by checking the original vouchers, interviewing and so on.
choiceNotes: Data analysis shows the situation within those data; it does not prove that a program has no errors.
The extracted transactions are candidates for examination, and whether they are fraudulent is judged through further checks.
Correct. Exceptional transactions can be extracted efficiently from all the records.

service-management-034.question: In a systems audit, which of the following does the systems auditor mainly use as the yardstick for judging whether an organization's management of its information systems is appropriate?
choices: System Management Standards
System Audit Standards
Audit working papers
service-management-034.explanation: In Japan, the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry publishes the System Audit Standards and the System Management Standards. The System Management Standards set out what an organization should do to manage its information systems properly, and systems auditors use them as the yardstick for audit judgments. The System Audit Standards set out the code of conduct for systems auditors when they carry out audits (how audits should be planned, performed, reported and so on). Audit working papers are documents recording the procedures the auditor carried out, the evidence obtained and the conclusions.
choiceNotes: Correct. They set out the management an organization should carry out and serve as the yardstick for audit judgments.
They set out the code of conduct for systems auditors, not a yardstick for judging whether management is appropriate.
These are documents recording the procedures and conclusions of the auditor, not a yardstick for judgment.

service-management-035.question: In the framework of Japan's internal control reporting system under the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act (J-SOX), which of the following is one of the four objectives of internal control?
choices: Increasing market share
Speeding up new product development
Safeguarding of assets
service-management-035.explanation: In the J-SOX framework, the objectives of internal control are four: effectiveness and efficiency of operations, reliability of reporting (including the reliability of financial reporting), compliance with laws and regulations related to business activities, and safeguarding of assets. This adds safeguarding of assets to the three objectives (operations, reporting and compliance) of the U.S. COSO framework. Increasing market share and speeding up development are business goals or strategies, not objectives of internal control.
choiceNotes: This is one of the business goals, not an objective of internal control.
This is a goal related to business strategy, not an objective of internal control.
Correct. Ensuring that assets are acquired, used and disposed of under proper procedures and approval is one of the objectives of internal control.

service-management-036.question: Among the basic components of internal control, which of the following describes the control environment appropriately?
choices: Identifying, analyzing and evaluating risks that hinder the achievement of the organization's objectives, and choosing responses to them

The component that sets the tone of the organization and is the foundation of all the other basic components, including management's integrity and ethical values, organizational structure, and assignment of authority and responsibility
Policies and procedures, such as approvals, reconciliations and segregation of duties, established so that management's orders and instructions are properly carried out
service-management-036.explanation: In the Japanese framework of internal control, there are six basic components: the control environment, risk evaluation and response, control activities, information and communication, monitoring, and response to IT (information technology). The control environment sets the tone of the organization, influences the control consciousness of the people in it, and is the foundation of the other basic components. It includes management's integrity and ethical values, management policies, the functioning of the board of directors and corporate auditors, organizational structure, assignment of authority and responsibility, and personnel policies.
choiceNotes: This describes risk evaluation and response.
Correct. It is the component that sets the tone of the organization and forms the foundation of the other basic components.
This describes control activities.

service-management-037.question: In internal control over purchasing, which of the following is an appropriate measure in line with segregation of duties?
choices: Having different people enter purchase order data and approve those orders
To make the work more efficient, having the same person handle ordering, receiving inspection and payment
So that staff transfers cause no trouble, giving everyone authority for all processing
service-management-037.explanation: Segregation of duties is the principle of dividing responsibilities and authority so that no single person can carry out a transaction alone from initiation through approval, recording and custody of assets. If input and approval are done by different people, errors and fraud cannot be completed by one person's decision and are easier to find through mutual checks. The same principle is applied in information systems, for example by separating the people who develop programs from those who operate the production environment.
choiceNotes: Correct. Separating input from approval means one person cannot complete an error or fraud alone.
If one person can handle everything from ordering to payment, it is hard to prevent fraud, such as fictitious orders, and errors.
This grants more authority than necessary, which goes against both segregation of duties and the principle of keeping authority to the necessary minimum.

service-management-038.question: Which of the following describes IT governance appropriately?
choices: The information systems department setting the procedures for day-to-day operation of servers and networks and carrying out the work exactly as those procedures say

The system in which management takes the lead in giving direction to the strategy for using IT, evaluating and monitoring its execution and results, to achieve the organization's goals and raise corporate value
The project manager managing the schedule, cost and quality of a development project by comparing actual results with the plan
service-management-038.explanation: IT governance is the system by which management (the board and other senior leadership) takes responsibility for directing IT investment and use, and for evaluating and monitoring its execution and results, so that the use of IT fits the organization's goals and strategy. The international standard ISO/IEC 38500 describes the role of the governing body as Evaluate, Direct and Monitor. Procedures for day-to-day operations and the management of individual projects are management activities carried out under the direction of IT governance.
choiceNotes: This is an activity of IT operations management, which differs from IT governance led by management.
Correct. Management takes the lead in directing the use of IT and evaluating and monitoring it.
This is an activity of project management.

service-management-039.question: Monitoring, a basic component of internal control, consists of ongoing monitoring and independent evaluations. Which of the following is an independent evaluation?
choices: The accounting section manager checks, as part of daily work, the results of the payment reconciliations carried out by subordinates
On the order entry screen, the system automatically checks the number of digits in amounts and the required fields
An internal audit department independent of the business periodically evaluates the status of the design and operation of internal control
service-management-039.explanation: Monitoring is the process of continuously evaluating whether internal control is working effectively. Ongoing monitoring is built into normal business activities and carried out continuously; checks by supervisors are an example. Independent evaluations are carried out periodically or as needed, separately from ongoing monitoring, from a standpoint independent of the business; evaluations by the internal audit department and audits by corporate auditors are examples. Input checks by the system are control activities (controls over business processing that use IT).
choiceNotes: This is a check by a supervisor within normal work, so it is ongoing monitoring.
This is an input check, a control activity that uses IT.
Correct. It is a periodic evaluation by a department independent of the business, so it is an independent evaluation.

service-management-040.question: Within the "response to IT" in internal control, which of the following is an IT general control?
choices: Changes to programs in the production environment are deployed to production only after approval and testing, and by a person other than the developer
On the order entry screen, an entry is rejected if the customer code is not registered in the master data
The system automatically calculates the invoice amount from the unit price and quantity
service-management-040.explanation: Controls in response to IT are divided into IT general controls and IT application controls. IT application controls are built into individual business systems and ensure that transaction data are processed correctly; input data checks and automatic calculations are examples. IT general controls maintain an environment in which application controls work effectively and cover system development and maintenance, operations management, access management, management of outsourcing and so on. Approval of program changes and separating development from deployment to production are IT general controls.
choiceNotes: Correct. Managing program changes and separating these duties are IT general controls.
This is an input data check, which is an IT application control.
This is an automatic calculation by the system, which is an IT application control.
